[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.21.0 - the Doomed Plateau[/b][/size]

Every act in the game is now surveyed, built and released, so this release asks a different question: does any
of it actually play better? For the Crypt and for England, the honest answer was no.

Measured by where the work landed rather than how much of it there was: the Crypt got eighteen parts across
eleven maps, of which [b]twenty-two of twenty-six dialogue placements are balloons with no replies[/b]. One
conversation. No merchant, no healer, and no change to what spawns. Its one genuine respite, the Garrison
Camp, is a dead-end side room hanging off the [i]first[/i] map and exiting only back to it - so you visit it before
the act begins, and then walk 2,783 spawn entries with nothing but narration. England is better and still
front-loaded: its Templar camp sits on maps 02 and 04 of eleven, and maps 03 and 05 through 09 received
nothing at all between them across 1,010 spawn entries.

A balloon on a corpse pile is a subtitle on the monotony. It makes the grind legible. It does not shorten it,
vary it, or make it optional.

[b]Captains instead[/b]

The Plateau is the Crypt's biggest fight - 1,055 spawn entries, more than a third of the act in one place -
and its problem was never a missing rest stop. It was fifty-six templates of the same thing. So the undead get
captains.

[b]The Bonecaller.[/b] The largest piece of finished-but-unfielded creature content this project has found is the
Boss Lich: three races, a sprite, and [b]seventeen animations[/b] - better animated than monsters the game
actually ships - and no character template anywhere pointing at any of it, so nothing could ever spawn one. Its
races are a designed encounter rather than a stat bump. An enormous pool at armour class 80, so it is trivial to
hit and very slow to fall; [b]immune to cold, poison and disease[/b]; hardening against electrical and piercing as
it tiers up; and fire left deliberately weakest at every tier.

It is also the one captain that can be reasoned with, because a lich commands and remembers. Wielder standing,
Divine magic or plain Speech will open it, and what you find is something bound to a siege whose author is long
dead: *"Something raised me and pointed me at a spear on the far side of those walls, and the pointing has
outlived the hand. I cannot put the order down."*

You can release it. It is retagged into the other army, the horde turns on it, and it is glad: *"I have raised
every one of them twice and I know exactly where the joints are."*

Or, if your karma is low enough, you can swear to it instead - promise it the Lance and break the keep's door
yourself. Then it walks in behind you, the Templar garrison turns on it, and the garrison's own offer to take
you in is closed for good: [i]"Are you a Knight? Have you been sent to reinforce us?"[/i] has no good answer left,
not even the lie. [b]Anyone may free it. Only the wicked may recruit it.[/b]

[b]The Bonewright.[/b] The Lance's second guardian shipped at roughly half its designed strength, because its cans
run on a generic ghoul stat block while its own race - HP 250/400/600, AC 175/215/300 - sat in the files used by
nothing. Restored. And it raises the fallen for as long as it stands, so the endless stream on that slope
finally has a source, and a lever: kill the standard-bearer and along the whole slope the half-risen settle,
and for the first time nothing new is getting to its feet.

[b]The Revenant Sergeant.[/b] This one has kept its rank. It opens the fight moving its section with two fingers
and [b]has not once looked at you, because you are not yet the problem[/b]. Bring it below two thirds and it
whistles its section off the knights and onto you. Below a third it drops the hand signals, abandons the battle
entirely, and comes for you alone through its own dead.

[b]What this release is not[/b]

It does not add a non-combat route through the Crypt, and it does not pretend to. Acts 4 through 7 are corridors
with no alternate exits, and that is a different kind of work. What it adds is three landmarks in the largest
fight in the act, one of which can be talked out of fighting you at all, and two of which behave in ways worth
noticing.

[b]Fixt[/b] is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt.

Download, unzip, run [i]Mod Manager.bat[/i]. This is level parts, so it needs a character who has not yet entered
the Doomed Plateau. Unplayed; what you find goes into 0.21.1. If you take the Lich's side, I would especially
like to know whether the garrison really turns on it.

https://github.com/EricHype/LionheartFixt/releases/tag/v0.21.0
